name: Arman Financial Services Ltd
title: Arman Financial Services Ltd - 531179 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Arman Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT rose to INR45 crore from a loss of INR15 crore a year ago, with AUM at a record INR2,925 crore (+36% YoY).
summary.overview: Consolidated disbursements of INR686 crore were up 76% YoY, the highest ever Q1, while cost-to-income improved to 44.3% from 51.7% in Q4 FY26. GNPA fell to 2.76% and NNPA to 0.84%, with collection efficiency at 96.6% for the quarter. Management repeatedly said the sector has not fully normalised and that volumes were below expectations, with a stated focus on quality over quantity. Namra Finance (microfinance) drove most of the profit improvement, and the individual loan book rose to 33% of the book.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR59 crore in Q4 FY26
vs loss of INR15 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR41 crore in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Arman Financial (standalone)
segments.commentary: AUM INR758 crore (+26% YoY, +4% QoQ); disbursements INR156 crore led by MSME; GTI INR66 crore (+30% YoY); PPOP INR24 crore; PAT INR15 crore (+17% YoY, +48% QoQ).

segments.name: Namra Finance (microfinance)
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,167 crore (+39% YoY, +8% QoQ); disbursements INR530 crore; GTI INR138 crore (+35% YoY); PPOP INR52 crore (+64% YoY); PAT INR30 crore vs loss of INR28 crore a year ago; NIM 15.37%; GNPA 2.59% from a peak of 3.8%.

guidance_outlook: Opex-to-AUM target of about 7% by end of FY27; management said the ratio was about 8% this quarter (vs about 9% last quarter) and expects further decline.

Management said FY27 AUM growth of about 25% to 30% was the context for questions, but did not itself restate the figure; growth to be 'careful, calibrated' and recalibrated to collections and delinquency trends.
Credit cost: Vivek Modi said credit cost is expected to stay about 3% to 3.5%; Aalok Patel said including CGFMU cost, 3% sounds about right, maybe 2.5%, and 2% if lucky.
Borrowing cost: approaching rating agencies for upgrades, expected to cut interest cost by about 20-30 bps.
No explicit ROA guidance; Aalok Patel said on a fully levered basis historically about 4.5% and around 3.5-4% at about 20% capital adequacy with current opex.
capex_capacity: Management said current infrastructure can support disbursements of INR750 crore per quarter; Q4 FY26 consolidated disbursements were cited at INR700 crore-plus, and microfinance alone at INR738 crore per the presentation.
Branch network cited by analyst at about 400-425 branches, up from about 275-280 in 2023; management did not dispute this.
CGFMU coverage: about 94% of eligible microfinance portfolio covered as of 30 June 2026.

Liquidity: INR286 crore across cash, liquid investments and undrawn CC limits; INR335 crore undrawn sanctions from existing lenders. Average liquidity about INR300 crore, roughly 1.5 months of repayments plus one month of disbursements.
Solar loans: about INR50 lakh per month in selected areas; zero NPAs so far; yield about 18-20%.
demand_pricing: Q1 volumes were below management's expectations; rejection rates remain relatively high by design.
Individual loans are 33% of the book; about 68-70% of individual-loan EMIs clear via eNACH/UPI by month-end, around 85% cashless in total, with about 14% collected in cash door-to-door.
Management said the individual book is performing better than JLG, while acknowledging the product is new and opex is the key issue.
LAP (loan against property) disbursement is well below the analyst's expected INR40-50 crore per quarter; management cited secured-lending competition from MFIs, SFBs, banks and fintechs.
Rates: management said it would consider cutting rates if the company were earning too much, but has not given it much thought; RBI scrutiny cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why remain cautious given favourable collection and delinquency data?
qa_highlights.answer: Aalok Patel said the data is favourable but rural income growth and jobs quality are concerning on the ground; he called it a little PTSD and said he has no reason to be pessimistic.

qa_highlights.question: Recoveries on written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi said about INR185 crore of pool written off over 24 months was sold to an ARC in March 2025; recovery on it this year is about 10%, and overall write-off recoveries are about 3-4%, with 12-18 months still to run.

qa_highlights.question: When will liquidity fall and disbursements pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquidity is already sufficiently low, averaging about INR300 crore, and described the current level as a 'Goldilocks' position; the team has been in collection mode for two years and volumes should recover over the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Yield, funding cost and opex outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is expected to fall toward 7% of AUM; funding cost of about 11.7% is expected to fall 20-30 bps on rating upgrades; on yields, management said it will reduce rates only if earnings become excessive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MSME 31-90 PAR and LAP GNPA rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi attributed about 10-15 bps of upward movement in MSME PAR to higher stress in Telangana, with other states stable; Aalok Patel said there were other reasons too.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost guidance and July collections?
qa_highlights.answer: July repayment rates were marginally lower than June, about 3 bps on zero DPD, attributed to rain in Gujarat, UP and Bihar; credit cost guided at about 3-3.5% by Vivek Modi, with management saying 2-3% is possible including CGFMU costs.

qa_highlights.question: ROA and individual loan economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it gives no formal ROA guidance; historically about 4.5% on a fully levered basis, and about 3.5-4% at 20% CAR on current opex. Individual loans are preferred but the product is still new.

risks_watch: Macro stress lag: management expects macro events may hit customer segments with a lag, and said rural income growth and job quality are concerns; July repayments were marginally lower than June (about 3 bps on zero DPD) on rain in Gujarat, UP and Bihar.
Telangana stress: MSME 31-90 PAR rose from about 0.7% to 0.9%, with management attributing about 10-15 bps to Telangana; other states stable, with other unspecified reasons also cited.
LAP growth: disbursements well below the analyst's expected INR40-50 crore per quarter, with competition from MFIs, SFBs, banks and fintechs in secured lending.

Credit cost and opex trajectory: credit cost guided loosely at 3-3.5% (2.5-3% including CGFMU per Aalok Patel); opex-to-AUM target of about 7% by end FY27 from about 8% this quarter; management said it had no set credit cost guidance.
Funding and rating upgrades: incremental borrowing cost about 11.7%; rating upgrade efforts expected to cut interest cost 20-30 bps; yield cuts only if earnings become excessive.

Volume recovery: management expects volumes to recover over the next couple of quarters; liquidity about INR300 crore average; write-off recoveries of about 3-4% with 12-18 months left on the ARC pool.
key_quotes: I would still hesitate to say that the sector has completely normalized.
Our rejection rates continue to remain relatively high, and we are comfortable with that.
I'm not scared. I'm still confident. It's just I don't want the same euphoria that happened post-COVID
I don't give any guidance on ROAs, very frankly.
summary.management_tone: Confident on reported numbers and collections but deliberately cautious on the cycle, repeatedly saying the sector has not normalised and that growth will be calibrated to collections. Evasive or non-committal on ROA, credit cost and rate cuts, which it declined to guide to firmly, and on LAP scaling, which it attributed to competition and time.

adds.what: Current infrastructure can support disbursements of INR750 crore per quarter (existing capacity, not new build)

growth.why: Q1 FY27 disbursements were INR686 crore against stated capacity of INR750 crore per quarter, but management said volumes ran below expectations and growth will be calibrated to collections and delinquency, with no explicit FY27 AUM growth guidance from management and no new capacity or capex disclosed.
